marks.gloss_en: R' Yehoshua: the morning Shema may be recited until three hours [of the day]
Israel said to Moses: if only we could get out ourselves [and ask for nothing]
R' Abbahu: why did Eliyahu say 'answer me' twice? it teaches that Eliyahu made two pleas before the Holy One
רבונו של עולם, דיה לצרה בשעתה -- sufficient is the trouble in its hour: do not announce the enslavement of the kingdoms to a people still in this one
Moshe: Master of the world, sufficient is the trouble in its hour [do not tell them now of a future enslavement]
the first instruction: go tell Israel -- I was with you in this enslavement, and I will be with you in the enslavement of the kingdoms
תניא נמי הכי: the vatikin completed the Shema with sunrise, to join redemption to prayer and pray by day
the baraita: the vatikin completed it with sunrise so as to join redemption to prayer and pray by day
מאי קראה -- ייראוך עם שמש: reverence offered 'with the sun', as the vatikin pray at sunrise
R' Zeira's verse for the vatikin: 'They shall fear You with the sun' (Ps 72:5)
one who reads from then on has not lost, like a man reading in the Torah
the rejected construal: distinguishing a white fleece from a techelet-dyed fleece (but those are told apart at night too)
R' Meir: from when one tells a wolf from a dog
Rav Huna: the halakha follows Acherim
whoever joins redemption to prayer is not harmed the whole day
R' Yochanan: at the start of the Amidah one says 'O Lord, open my lips', and at its end 'let the words of my mouth find favour'
R' Elazar's first placement: the introductory verse belongs at the evening prayer (retracted)
R' Yochanan: one joins the redemption of evening to the evening prayer -- the dictum that refutes the first placement
R' Elazar's second placement: the verse belongs at the afternoon prayer
Rav Ashi: say it even at all of them -- once the Sages fixed the verse in the prayer it counts as one long prayer
the parallel that carries Rav Ashi's answer: hashkivenu was instituted as one long redemption blessing
R' Ami: 'and they lent them' (Ex 12:36) teaches that they lent them against their will
the one who says 'against the Egyptians' will': as it is written, 'and she who tarries at home divides the spoil' (Ps 68:13)
R' Ami: 'and they emptied Egypt' teaches that they made it like a trap with no grain in it
